name: soft tissue mass overview
title: A soft tissue mass: under 5 cm with no suspicious feature is excised; over 5 cm or with any suspicious feature is imaged and core-biopsied first, then a benign result is observed, a resectable sarcoma is staged and treated by surgery with radiation, and a non-curable one goes to palliative care

root.title: A soft tissue lump: could it be a SARCOMA? Decide BEFORE anyone cuts it out
lines: benign tumours are 100 times more common · a sarcoma shelled out like a benign lump, with little or no margin, is the 'WHOOPS'

groups.title: Over 5 cm, OR under 5 cm with ANY suspicious feature
lines: rapid growth · pain · recurrent · deep · fixed · difficult location

pres.title: IMAGE before biopsy
lines: MRI preferred · CT · rarely ultrasound · or a surgical expert
then CORE biopsy by someone experienced in sarcoma · NOT fine needle aspiration

head: h
Low risk
inv: complete removal with minimal surrounding tissue

head: h
Benign on biopsy
e.g. spindle cell/pleomorphic lipoma
inv: immunohistochemistry: MDM2 negative, CD34 positive → lipoma

head: h
Sarcoma, resectable
usually a PAINLESS lump
inv: the lung is where it spreads
tx: • curable with it: osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma in young adults

head: h
Not curable
e.g. lung metastases, non-resectable
inv: no standard chemotherapy · goals of care · clinical trials
tx: can greatly improve quality of life

panels.title: History and exam
items: has it GROWN? when first noticed, how big then and now (compare to fruit or nuts)
pain or numbness: sarcomas are usually painless; significant symptoms → think metastases · recurrence · other lumps · family history
superficial (subcutaneous) or deep (muscle) · mobile, tethered or fixed · nodes rarely involved
